name: Alcohol avoidance (sober maxxing)

lead: Sober maxxing is quitting or abstaining from alcohol, in appearance communities often to get clearer, less puffy skin and better sleep.

Abstaining removes ethanol and its metabolite acetaldehyde, which is linked to flushing and DNA damage. Reported benefits of sustained abstinence include better sleep, reversal of early fatty liver disease and lower blood pressure. No published study has measured facial appearance specifically after quitting.

paras: People stop drinking entirely, often replacing it with non-alcoholic drinks, and track sleep and skin over weeks to months. Many pair it with other routines such as training and a regular sleep schedule.

Alcohol is an IARC Group 1 carcinogen, and the WHO has stated that no level of alcohol consumption is free of health risks. Withdrawal in dependent drinkers can be dangerous, so heavy drinkers should not stop abruptly without medical advice.

angle.text: Sober maxxers quit alcohol to get clearer, less puffy skin and better sleep, since poor sleep and alcohol's effects both show on the face. Sleep gains and liver recovery after quitting are documented; facial appearance after quitting has not been measured.

lead: Alcohol avoidance, sometimes called sober maxxing, is the practice of quitting or abstaining from alcohol, in appearance communities often for the stated aim of improving skin.

The IARC classifies ethanol as a Group 1 carcinogen, and the WHO has stated that no level of alcohol consumption is free of health risks.[1] Reported benefits of sustained abstinence include better sleep, reversal of early fatty liver disease and lower blood pressure.[1] No published study was found testing alcohol abstinence for facial appearance.

sections.h: Health effects of alcohol and abstinence
paras: Alcohol raises the risk of oesophageal, mouth, liver and breast cancers, and with tobacco accounts for about 72% of head and neck cancers.[1] The WHO estimates about 2.6 million deaths a year from alcohol (2019 data).[1]

After sustained abstinence, sleep quality often improves, early fatty liver disease can reverse, blood pressure and heart rhythm can stabilise, and cancer risk declines; people also report clearer thinking and less anxiety.[1]

The alcohol flush reaction, facial or body redness from acetaldehyde buildup, is common in people of East Asian descent and linked to an ALDH2 variant.[1] The sources reviewed do not cover rosacea or other skin conditions and appearance.
Proponents describe quitting alcohol as part of a skin and health routine. The sources reviewed give no appearance outcome data.
No studies found on alcohol abstinence for facial appearance.
